### 2026-10-08 – OCTOBER 7TH - Made an Idea and it failed badly

**7.9h**

OCTOBER 7TH - Made an Idea and it failed badly

This entry has been posted on october 9th but all the hours for this entry were accumulated october 7th.
I am a total beginner in PCB making. Before I started recording I read through countless files and watched a ton of tutorials (I am not counting the youtube watching hours). This was done to prepare myself and give myself an idea of what I'm doing. I learned how to set up the timelapses and hackatime-that was the easy part!

non time lapsed hours (2) spent conceptualizing my idea plus making physical notes and researching how the parts would go together

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/afcd8b4a42af97929868fdd46a5dc72d749f98cc1faf635987adf68d5490da3d.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/6ee2ae1b07014f6d58b1bcff8fdf32f6eb37d30bee48dc51f2e62117ac6075b5.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/4c05622a5ff70efc9214dd5ede6adc995ecbb80c6b79c020129e421379ca4ab8.png)

Those Images served as a guide for me when i tried moving forward and i'm so glad i took the time to do it. They aren't easy to understand but my brain understands them perfectly. It made understanding PCBs a bit easier. The drawing process was filled with research on how each component would fit on the pcb. that hour also made me realize that my previous understanding of PCBs was entirely wrong.
The links that helped me:
https://docs.kicad.org/8.0/en/getting_started_in_kicad/getting_started_in_kicad.html
https://github.com/pablov55/Beginner-s-Guide-to-KiCad/blob/main/README.md

Non time lapsed hours (2) - Electronic Lab visit + aerobot schematic assembly (massive fail)
I went to the lab for an interactive schematics tutorial i booked at the electronics lab. Since i have access to the lab i decided to try it. I soon realized I was being overly ambitious. This idea was way beyond my experience and too complex for a beginner. I spent 2 hours trying to wire up the schematics, despite my tutors input, i just couldn't bring my idea to life. At the end of the session he suggested focusing on a simpler project. I did make sme progress, I had a better understanding of the KiCad software functions!

An image of me at the lab (i learned a lot about voltage, decoupling and resistors and capacitors)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/4f9c0d7074440baa50710b2a7db6c07dfaf7459841b0a0205eb0ef32ede6d11d.png)

My overly ambitious fail before my slightly less ambitious fail:

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 134425](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/49ad3da2a2805b8715cd7b2111190a69e17a6ee5f129e5b7a6bb3104e44e1a48.png)

Special feature:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/fd57e5d646675427245f0ee299a6c97b32976fc9b19a2eb9efba59473a7f27ae.png)

The image above caused me so many problems both on and off screen. I wanted to use that ESP32-S3 board but none of the parts on KiCad fit it perfectly. This consumed so much of my time because i kept trying to understand how to edit it or maybe even make my own esp32 on KiCad forthe specific one i wanted to use. I also searched multiple sites to find an esp32 that would fit the lay out that was available on KiCad but that failed. That period forced me out of my comfort zone, I went out of my ways to brainstorm different methods (The answer was simple, I didn't have any external schematic or footprint libraries installed, which is why i couldn't find most things I kept seeing in guides. I didn't come to this conclusion during the session so i continued working blindly)

Looking back, I'm really not sure of what I was trying to achieve. I didn't understand how anything worked but somehow I thought I did. This is future me speaking now that everything i learned has settled in. My mistake was that i thought every component i wanted to add had it's own symbol. I continued with this mindset for a while which is why i spent an unhealthy amount of time on such a simple looking schematic.

Hours that were timelapsed:
I just feel like reflecting on these hours too but they arent counted for anything. I started a proper timelapse when i got home. At first I was still stubborn and tried forcing all th ideas i had for the aerobot into one complex creation but it didnt work so i started again. The timelapse shows that. I also got frustrated and started trying to set my github and codespace up properly. I did this because these things are necessary before my project can be shipped, so although this did count toward the project, i wish i did it later because it stressed me out. I still have some work to do on my repositories because some things don't sync properly but for the most part, I finally learned how to organise a repository as well as create a codespace and install the firmware extension on my vs code. It is still a mess but I belive this mess will contribute to a more presentable project when I'm ready to ship. I also learned to link my hackatime. I wanted to edit out the points in my timelapse when I wasn't being productive but it failed to cut out so there is around an hour that isn't dedicated to the project. It's all related in some way, but the half life rules state that those activites don't count

Overall, this session was bought both stressful and enlightining. In the next session, I made way more progress though I started out with some struggles I experienced in the first session too, having experience the first session made it a bit easier to overcome

### 2026-10-09 – JUNE 8TH - Struggled a lot, almost gave up, then locked in and finished the schematics

**5.92h**

JUNE 8TH - Struggled a lot, almost gave up, then locked in and finished the schematics

This session taught me a lot about PCBs and electronics. I had to go through a bunch of repositories and other people's works, as well as, get help from ai in order to get to where I am now. The ai was pretty frustrating but it was still helpful for a beginner. As i progressed, I used less of it because it isn't too helpful when you actually know what to do and how to bring your idea into reality. I still use it for shaping my ideas into achievable things because I tend to be overly ambitious.
This is what I was working with at first:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/24c9d9225659b757f9b3cd45eb79fad277df3629391e64612262282b2218146c.png)

The idea was to make do with the esp32 symbol that was available and most similar to the one i wanted to get. This made me go through a back and forth experience for a while. I really struggled here.

Thankfully, I joined a half life huddle while i was working and someone told me I needed to install the library on the starbie repo.

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 232539](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/fe6680ddf09e45701fe41d68e2de3708fedc397de115fe83549fb41553b10d62.png)

With that, I was able to gain a clear understanding of what pcb making is actually about and landed on this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 235717](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/0cb10973e5933728a188f9bedfc372dad487a3014f598b024419410dde3876be.png)

I really wanted some extra features but I think It's a bit too complex for me right now. I might try again in my next session.
I want to add this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 002319](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/91c1342fe7ebd3c913251d4e7d2b56cd5db044641a25182c2bc3434e0505d0c5.png)

But i'm not sure how its gonna fit on the board (look at the image below) and i don't want stuff poking out of my aerobot

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 002926](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/ee45a9e5fce273be700428cf8a79735780b83fdb147b93d8110733233e21eb9f.png)

I might try regular leds because I want to use the leds to indicate battery power and maybe any other function that I'm able to program unto the esp32.
I learned a lot from this session and i also have a cleared idea and path for creating the perfect aerobot.
Next, I'll work on the footprints and brainstorm ideas of what I want to program unto my esp32, reconsider the led, and research how to make the aerobot super interactive even though i don't have lots of coding knowledge. I love half life because it's pushing me to learn things I never thought I would be able to do
I'll also work on my read me since i have an understanding of what i want to do now, and perfect/clean up my git hub.

### 2026-10-09 – June 9th  - Even more progress

**9.57h**

June 9th  - Even more progress

I spent lots of time sourcing the parts. I had to find the ones with compatible drivers, as well as, the right size.
I learned about oled types and pin types during this search.
I had some doubts on my schematics so i kept researching and that took lots of time.Then i decided to go from an esp32-s3 plus to the standard. This mde things a bit easier to understand.
I took some time off screen to sketch the sizes and research the components better. This helped me to understand the dimensions and arrangements I'd apply to my actual pcb:
Here is a the final result of the non time lapsed work I did:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/0f95a9eb5e73320d009a9a6629612680402c198ef4e23481827d31c0ffe90e65.png)

it took me around over an hour because I had to check reviews and also find the driver type and dimensions of the parts so i could map it out properly and plan acccordingly. I mapped it out on paper before any actual pcb design. Doing this was really helpful and it pushed me in the right direction, I had an old esp32 laying around and i decided to try to visualise a new idea i had but it didn't work out as i hoped. This was what i was working with:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/qPcmVml5icKkARKbagHZd2brr6lkJ2Kc/84934175f019a35c60b951883e9ab564d8e3411d8c26f44e7f0575884b2a3e77.png)

Nonetheless, I still learned a lot during while i researched the components, made the outline and tested my ideas with a breadboard.

After that I countinued recording. I had a better understanding of the components i'd use so I updated my read me. That was quite fun. Then i had to search for the components all over again because i used the wrong amazon chain (I forgot i had to use amazon.co.uk). I ended up switching to aliexpress.

Later, I tried to tweak my project a bit more but it all failed, I removed th battery socket because i wasn't sure how to make it charge without frying the esp32 pins. I also wanted to add an sd card slot but it added unnecessary complications. I tried the battery thing again and this time it seemed possible but then i got advise on half life help and it became clear that i really didn't know how to make this work, but that's okay. It's all part of the process.
I decided to go for a simpler route after that.
I went on a half life huddle after I finished the schematics. There, a kind individual helped me find the right footprints. I didn't know what to do after i finished my schematics but he helped me figure everything out step by step. After that, I started arranging my pcb, i learned how to view it in 3d too!

Im 80% done. There's much to do but so much has already been done. I feel way more confident in my pcb design skills now.

All that's left is to route it properly, and then add some designs to make it mine,

My esp32 might have limited functions. Btw, I switched to the esp32-c3 for extra simplicity. But yes, i won't be going overboard on it because I am also new to programming and I have classes to attend to. This journey has opened me to a whole new world and I look forward to doing more and learning to manage my time with classes and electronics in my free time
